newsitem.title: UK: Sleaze shows weak Major leadership-UK Labour.
newsitem.headline: Sleaze shows weak Major leadership-UK Labour.

text.p: The main opposition Labour party said on Thursday that a spate of sleaze allegations against ruling Conservative party members of parliament showed the weak leadership of Prime Minister John Major.

A day after ex-minister Tim Smith quit as a candidate over his failure to declare accepting cash for asking questions in parliament, Labour's Gordon Brown challenged the Consevative high command to answer questions about the suitability of other candidates "where there are known and admitted facts".
"This has now moved beyond a question of the behaviour of Tory MPs to a question of leadership," Brown, Labour's economics spokesman, told a news conference.

"The weakness of John Major's leadership is now a key issue. His failure to control his party. His failure to take action against the MPs who asked questions for money. His broken promises," Brown added.
Labour also challenged Major to rule out increasing value added tax on domestic fuel if it retains power at the May 1 election.

It attacked the Conservatives for breaking a promise it made at the 1992 election by introducing VAT on home power bills in 1993. Since then, Brown said, the typical British familiy had paid 197 pounds in VAT on fuel.
"The Tories say one thing before an election, they do another after. No one can trust them on VAT again," Brown said.
